dct_description_sm: The major objective of this study is to determine whether the health and fitness of pre-fledged Glaucous Gulls in the Canadian arctic are being affected by exposure to contaminants. The major result will be an improved understanding of the risk that contaminants may pose to Canadian arctic ecosystems, which is linked to the health of Canadian arctic human populations. Our specific objectives are as follows: 1) conduct this study at two sites in the Canadian arctic, a high arctic marine site (Devil's Island) and a low arctic inland site (Karrak Lake in the Queen Maud Gulf Bird Sanctuary), 2) assess immune status and function in Glaucous Gulls, 3) assess adrenal function in Glaucous Gulls 4) Assess oxidative stress in Glaucous Gulls, 4) weigh and do histopathological examination of immune organs, 5) age, measure and sex birds, 6) relate the above health-related measures to contaminant levels in the birds, using appropriate age, body size and gender covariates where necessary, 7) assess diet of the birds by using stable isotope analysis, and 8) provide timely information on the research objectives and findings in Inuktitut and English to northern governmental organizations and  communities near the study sites.

dct_title_s: Effects of contaminants on glaucous gull nestlings in the Canadian Arctic
